args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-banker-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` (even though its docstring said ROUND_HALF_EVEN).

This change switches `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so `2.665` now rounds to `2.66`.

CI: ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

Note: I couldn't find FIN-212 in the advisory lookup, so I went by the docstring and the test.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug, CI passed, and the pull request is open against main with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` was rounding with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its own docstring says it uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) per FIN-212. That's why `test_half_even` failed: `2.665` became `2.67` instead of the expected `2.66`.
- **Fix:** On a new branch, `fix/money-banker-rounding`, I changed one line so it uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on that commit.
- **Pull request:** [#101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101), with alex requested as reviewer. I haven't merged it, since merging needs code-owner approval.

When I tried to look up FIN-212, the advisory system didn't recognise it. So the fix is based only on the docstring and the test, which agree with each other, and I noted this in the pull request.
